title: The TWO different completion gates of Prompt Two, kept separate on purpose
coverage: Both gates extracted verbatim and individually numbered: unit predicate 12/12, program stopping rule 21/21. State assessment: 21/21 conditions assigned a verdict (0 TRUE, 14 FALSE, 7 NOT-CHECKED). Counts recomputed mechanically by .probe_selfcheck.py, which caught and corrected three hand-counting errors in an earlier draft of this file.
why_this_file_exists: These two gates are frequently conflated. They are different objects with different scopes, different condition counts and different consumers. The UNIT predicate answers 'is this ONE work unit done?' and runs at EVERY fan-in. The PROGRAM stopping rule answers 'may the whole program stop?' and runs once. Program condition 21 embeds the unit predicate, which is the only place they touch.

source_spec.line_numbering: LF-only (sed/grep/CI compatible). Path.read_text() inflates these numbers by up to 166 because the file carries 166 BARE CR bytes that universal-newline translation converts into line breaks.
source_spec.extraction_probe: data.split(b'\n') then regex '^(\\d+)\\.\\s+(.*)$' from each section header. Detector control: a known-present anchor returned a hit and a known-absent anchor returned [] before any count was trusted.

gate_a_unit_completion_predicate.name: One completion predicate everywhere
gate_a_unit_completion_predicate.used_at: every fan-in - local runners, cloud dispatchers, monitors, harvesters, workflow fan-in, cross-vendor adapters, and final synthesis (spec line 10648). One SHARED reducer, not a reimplementation per caller.
hard_rules: Exit code zero alone is never success (spec line 10646).
A plausible digest is not a receipt (spec line 10646).
A file path in text is not proof the file exists (spec line 10646).

gate_b_program_stopping_rule.name: Completion and stopping rule
gate_b_program_stopping_rule.quantifier: ALL of the following must be true
gate_b_program_stopping_rule.preamble: 'Infinite' does not mean looping forever. Continue until evidence-based convergence (spec line 11374).
gate_b_program_stopping_rule.failure_protocol: If something cannot be completed, do not hand-wave. Produce a TWO-SIGNAL proof of the blocker, preserve partial artifacts, state the exact missing prerequisite, and continue all independent work that remains possible (spec line 11400).

conflation_warnings: Gate A has 12 conditions and is per-unit; gate B has 21 and is per-program. Citing '12 conditions' for program completion or '21' for a work unit is the conflation this file exists to prevent.
They intersect at exactly ONE point: gate B condition 21 invokes gate A. Nowhere else does a gate-A condition imply a gate-B condition or vice versa.

Gate A condition 7 ('required tests ran and passed') is NOT gate B condition 4 ('no required test is red'). A unit can pass its own tests while a program-required gate is red - which is the state today.
Gate A condition 10 ('no unresolved P0/P1 defect is ATTACHED' - to this unit) is NOT gate B condition 3 ('ALL P0/P1 defects are closed' - program-wide).
